title: Round 12 / algorithm inventor B
question: Representation-change algorithms: invent ECDLP algorithms that move the instance to a different representation or object (alternative curve models, x-only/Kummer arithmetic, isogeny walks, covers, structured maps to other groups or to algebraic systems) where the scalar becomes cheaper to recover, escaping the lab's transfer and isogeny-invariance barriers; prototype and benchmark against Pollard rho.

sources.title: Jao, Miller, Venkatesan - Do all elliptic curves of the same order have the same difficulty of discrete log?
Galbraith - Climbing and Descending Tall Volcanos (ePrint 2024/924), as listed in search result
sources.locator: search-result snippet only; paper not read

claims: B1 (Aut-orbit rho) recovers k on j=0 and j=1728 toy curves (r up to 2^36); measured exponents 0.44-0.49 (CIs contain 0.5); pooled ratio vs plain rho 1.45 [1.14,1.88] (j=0, rule: NO ADVANTAGE) and 2.62 [2.15,3.17] (j=1728, rule: CONSTANT-FACTOR); known technique, no asymptotic claim.

B2 (2-isogeny volcano ascent to j=0 then B1) recovers k on 150/150 instances; ascent cost O(log^2 p) isogeny evaluations (slope vs a 1.86); applies to ~p^-0.47 [-0.58,-0.38] of curves (T3); constant-factor only; known in kind (JMV 2005, Galbraith 2024).

Pre-registered rule output 'asymptotic improvement' for B2 with W=10 is judged a false positive (additive polylog overhead plus heavy-tailed rho baseline); no speedup over sqrt(r) is claimed for any candidate. Empirical evidence only; no proof.
next_action: Do not pursue B1/B2 for sub-sqrt(r); optionally measure distance-to-structure (class size H(t^2-4p)) to confirm the sqrt(p) obstacle; amend the slope-based decision rule (additive overheads, heavy-tailed rho) before reuse.
notes: Configured model claude-sonnet-5-5; runtime identity of subagents is not exposed to the PI. Self-reported model identity: claude-sonnet-5-5 (not runtime-verified). Executed via algorithm-engineering adapter following algorithm-inventor role.
